# Utah Mountain Luxury Management

This is a private operations dashboard for short-term rentals (Ranch House, Lindon House, River House) and a construction project. Live: https://wilhite-portfolio.pages.dev

## For browser agents (Grok / Cursor)

1. Read `/api/agent/map` (JSON) or this file.
2. Prefer **hash routes** or `window.UML.navigate(...)` over clicking the top nav. Overlay widgets can intercept clicks.
3. After login, `document.documentElement.dataset.umlTab` is the current screen.
4. Primary controls use `data-bot="..."` attributes.

### Hash routes

- `#/overview` — portfolio. When saved bookings could not be read, the home page still names the next event and the rate rules, with no price, and it does not raise a night. It also says a direct request stays off and the quote does not ask for a name. It also says whether Ranch and Lindon quiet hours are in effect in Utah. The River House guide does not name a clock. The River House is not on an event that ends before November 1. A house tab names the next event that house can quote. The page says how many door codes open tomorrow, with no names and no codes. The occupancy file includes a calendar block even when it is not listed as a stay. Names stay off that file. Downloading does not change a booking. The turnover list names checkout time, when the next stay starts, when that door code opens, when the next stay covers a named event, how many guests the next booking names, including children when the note names them and they fit inside that guest total, whether the next stay named an arrival time, whether this checkout named a departure time, whether a 2:00 PM leave is open for that checkout, whether the next stay can arrive at 1:00 PM, whether that stay can request the hot tub or a grocery drop, and the guest's quiet hours. When two or three houses check out on the same day, the list says whether those same-day turns overlap. A 1:00 PM arrival and a 2:00 PM leave can fit one after the other when both houses are in Lindon. A River House turn on that day is not treated as that fit, because the drive up Provo Canyon is not in the clock. The co-host brief uses that same clock. Nothing is booked or sent. Names and the code stay off the list. Download occupancy lists taken nights and leaves names off the file. The list does not change a booking.
- `#/calendar` — tape chart for Ranch, Lindon, and the River House, whole and in three wings. Read only. A gap opens the market studio. It does not book a night.
- `#/market` — the next 12 months mark booked nights, closed nights, and whether an open night sits inside, above, or below the sample comp band. A comp saved with a sleep count and a distance reaches the rate band, and the saved ask for that night replaces the sample; a night no saved comp watched keeps the sample, and the page says which source set the band. A comp without a sleep count or a distance stays out. The page also lists each saved comp as a card with its area, distance, and observed ask, says when a comp has no saved ask, and lets the host save a comp by URL, label, sleep count, and distance; a save without a sleep count or a distance is refused. Named events from the rate card sit on the month, with no price. Each month also says the shortest stay, and a longer count when some nights ask for more. The cells do not show a price. When the calendar could not be read, the months do not say which nights are booked or open, the daily text does not raise a night, and the house panel does not list raises. When the calendar is live, the length and add-on lines stop before a closed night that is not listed as booked. The other-houses line uses an arrival that skips that night. Nothing is sent. The 30, 60, and 90 night share does not use a stand-in, and that card does not count a raise. The seven-day shadow clock that authorizes a Hospitable write is saved on the server, so clearing a browser tab cannot reset the week; a day that could not read the calendar removes its date, and a digest that could be sent is refused. Reading the clock does not return the write token. The page also shows what a rate push would change, built from the same shadow run: a booked, closed, paused, locked, or held night is never in it, and the plan is refused with a named reason while the week or the token is missing. That route has no writer, so nothing can be sent from it. The desk still states the rate rules: floor, ceiling, an 8% daily cap, and the published base is not lowered. That line has no price. A typed ask can still be judged against those rules. The same ask is also judged for River, Ranch, and Lindon. Those lines have no price. The night is not raised, and the line does not say the night is booked or open. Nothing is posted. A one-night start that fails a published rule names that rule. The line still has no price. The next seven nights from the rate card say the shortest start, or that the house has not started. The same seven nights also name River, Ranch, and Lindon together. When the calendar has been read, a closed night is marked closed even when it is not listed as booked. A night whose shortest stay would run into a booked or closed night says no start. The market page also lists each upcoming named event and the shortest stay each house can quote. That list has no price and does not say a house is open. Nothing is posted. That list has no price and does not say which nights are booked or open. None of those nights are raised. While the calendar cannot be read, the ask, the comp median, the rate band, and each sample’s weekend ask stay off the page. The sample comps can be sorted by distance, rating, sleeps, or reviews. A pin stays first. The sort stays in this tab, and nothing is posted. Fair only keeps the samples that sleep close and sit within 10 miles. That view stays in this tab, and it does not change the rate band. When the calendar is live, a night that no stay can cover keeps the published rate. It is not raised and it is not promoted. A typed ask on that night does not become a new base. Add-ons are named and the stay agreement is listed. Both are already on our page. Photos and card payment stay open. The nightly brief and the market page name that the River House still uses a rendering, and that Ranch and Lindon each have one photo. Direct booking still emails a request. Nothing is posted. The quote reads booked nights and a pace word from a nights-only calendar. Guest names, payouts, and notes stay off that response. Nothing is written. When the calendar has been read, a length on that check-in does not say the house is open. Choosing one does not send a request. When the calendar is live, the daily text says how many sample comps sleep close enough to set the band. That day does not count toward a rate push. A sample that sleeps under 60% of the house, or sits more than 10 miles away, stays on the list and stays out of the rate band when at least four samples are close and nearby. Sample comps on the page are counted for amenities. An item our guide already lists is marked as ours. A sample item the guide does not list stays a gap. Hiding a comp changes the count. The comps are not live listings, and nothing is posted. The page still shows the top 10 comps, a 90-day rate band, the same open arrivals as the booking page, the lengths the first arrival can quote, and the add-ons that arrival can request, with no prices. The unsent daily text names the next event on the rate card, with no price, and names those lengths and add-ons when the calendar is live, where the booking calendar asks for a longer start than the rate card, and which other houses will quote that arrival. That comparison has no prices. When reservations have loaded, the text says which stays name a party size and which name children. When the calendar is live, it also names the checkouts in the next two weeks and whether a 2:00 PM leave or a 1:00 PM arrival is open. When preference cards have loaded, it says which name an arrival time and which checkouts name a departure time. Names stay off those lines. Sample comps until live comps are connected. A calendar block stays closed and is not counted as a booked night. The 30, 60, and 90 night share leaves those blocks out of the sellable nights. It does not change Airbnb or VRBO rates. The board reads the overview when the response is JSON. A pinned or hidden comp stays on the set in this browser. A response that is not JSON stays on the sample board. Nothing is posted. When the calendar has been read, a named event whose start is booked is named and stays off the quote link. On a quote for both houses, that event follows a night booked at either house. The nights-ahead line counts a booked night at either house. Lindon stays off that count. Nothing is posted.
- `#/agents` — nightly brief from the calendar and the shadow clock. The desk on this page answers the Ranch and River split and the rate rules, with no price and no ledger amount. It also says how many sample comps sleep close and sit within 10 miles. That answer does not change the rate band. The public house list does not. The desk also names sample amenity gaps. A comp pinned in this browser changes that gap on the host desk. The public house guide does not. Those are not live listings, and they do not change the rate band. The nightly brief names the top gap for each house. It also names the next seven nights on the rate card for River, Ranch, and Lindon. That list has no price. When the calendar has been read, booked nights and calendar blocks are marked. A closed night is marked closed even when it is not listed as booked. A night whose shortest stay would run into a booked or closed night says no start. When it has not, the list does not say which nights are booked or open. Nothing is raised. The desk answers a rate-card week the same way and does not quote a price. It also names an outdoors day or a Sunday note from the published guide. That day has no price. Nothing is sent. Asked for upcoming events, the desk lists each named event and the shortest stay each house can quote. That answer has no price. Nothing is sent. A party larger than one house is told how many stay at the River House and how many stay at the Ranch House. That line has no price. A question about what to do before arrival names those published steps. Those steps have no price. Nothing is sent. A comp hidden on the market page changes that gap and how many sample comps sleep close enough to set the band. It has no price. The desk can also name the lengths a check-in can quote from the rate card. That list does not say the house is open, and nothing is charged yet. It can also name the shortest stay on a named event. That does not say the house is open. A pet question does not invent a rule. A party stays off the request. A numbered party is matched to the sleep count, and a party larger than one house is told that Ranch and River together sleep 45. A children question says children count toward the overnight guests, and a stay needs an adult. Nothing is sent. An insurance question and a cancel question use the stay agreement. When saved bookings could not be read, the brief does not raise or promote a night. It still names the next event and how many sample comps set each house’s band, and the published ask stays. It also states the Ranch and River split, including that a hot tub request and a grocery drop follow that split, with no ledger amount. The overview, report, owner statement, cleaner desk, and house pages do not show a stand-in list. Otherwise it includes where Ranch and River stays still on the books were booked, keeping the source name when it is not Airbnb or VRBO, the next open stretch, the next open arrival, the lengths that arrival can quote, the add-ons that arrival can request, where the booking calendar asks for a longer start than the rate card, how many door codes open tomorrow, and what the guest was asked to do before checkout. Codes stay off the brief. The brief names the stay agreement. The brief also names the River House toilet-paper step and the Ranch House hot-tub cover. The Lindon House keeps the shared checkout list. Nothing is sent. A pinned sample comp changes that brief. These stay sample comps. Nothing is posted. and does not sign it. It also says which other houses will quote the next open arrival, with no prices. A blocked night stays off the stretch and the arrival. Checkout lines name 11:00 AM and how many guests the next booking names. Names stay off. It does not claim jobs. A house-guide desk answers from the published guide, including the street address and how long a same-day turn is. It does not send a message or quote a price.
- `#/report` — P&L report. When saved bookings could not be read, the management figures stay off the page and it does not use a stand-in list. Documents stay available.
- `#/owner` — Todd’s Ranch and River statement. A read-only link can be made here. The link opens `/owner/<token>` with the Ranch and River share after the fee, each house’s stays, host payout, costs, and Todd’s share, and the month lines. Lindon, household, and construction stay off that page, and it has no download, no edit, and no guest names. A link that is not saved says so and shows no figure. Making a link does not email it, and a paused read says so instead of showing a stand-in statement. Nothing is booked, and a saved expense is not changed. The split is stated with no ledger amounts: 20% management fee to Brandon first, then half of what remains to Todd, including a loss. A hot tub request at the Ranch House and a grocery drop at the River House follow that same split. The card does not say that anyone asked, and it does not charge either one. An early arrival and a later checkout on Ranch or River follow that same split and wait until the calendar can be read. The card also names the same-day clean for Ranch and River: 5 hours from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM, or 2 hours when a 1:00 PM arrival or a 2:00 PM leave is named. It does not say that anyone asked. Lindon is not on that line. Nothing was booked or sent. The card also lists the next Ranch and River checkout mornings. Lindon is not on that list. This is not the statement. Names stay off the list. Nothing was booked or sent. A Ranch or River stay that names only children says a stay needs an adult. Names stay off that line. The card also states the rate rules: floor, ceiling, an 8% daily cap, and the published base is not lowered. That line has no price, and nothing is posted. The card also lists the next seven Ranch and River nights from the rate card. Lindon is not on that list. The list has no price. When the calendar has been read, booked nights and calendar blocks are marked. A closed night is marked closed even when it is not listed as booked. A night whose shortest stay would run into a booked or closed night says no start. When it has not, the list does not say which nights are booked or open. That card stays up when saved bookings could not be read. The statement stays off until those bookings can be read. Nothing was written over them. That card also says a direct request stays off and the quote does not ask for a name. A Ranch amount and a River amount are added before the fee. Upcoming events name the shortest Ranch and River stay from the rate card. A quoted stay links to that house page. The link does not hold the dates and does not invent a party. Lindon is not on that list. The card names the stay agreement guests read before a direct request: the house as-is, and that belongings are not insured. This page does not sign it. Nothing is charged yet. That trial is not the statement, and it does not read saved bookings. Read only. Download saves that same statement. A count of stays still on the books says where they were booked, keeps the source name when it is not Airbnb or VRBO, and names the next open stretch. A stretch no stay can cover is not called open. The next open arrival lists the lengths it can quote and the add-ons it can request, with no prices. It also names where the booking calendar asks for a longer start, with no prices, and that list is not in the spreadsheet. The next checkout names when the following stay starts, when that door code opens, whether the preference card names a departure time, and whether a 2:00 PM leave is open for that checkout. The code stays off, and that line is not in the spreadsheet. Stays that begin in the next 90 days are listed with the night count, whether the booking says how many guests, including children when the note names them, whether the preference card names an arrival time, whether a 1:00 PM arrival is open, whether that stay can request the hot tub or a grocery drop, and whether the stay covers a named event. Nothing extra is added for the event. Names and prices stay off, and that list is not in the spreadsheet. A blocked night stays off that stretch. Names stay off, and the count is not in the spreadsheet. Lindon and household bills are not on it. When the calendar has been read, a named event whose start is booked is named and stays off the quote link. Nothing is charged yet.
- `#/clean` — can make a link per cleaner. It opens `/clean/<token>` with no login and shows the next two weeks: the house, the day, what to do, how to get in, and the house rules, in English or Spanish, with the 4pm deadline first on a same-day turn. The cleaner ticks each step and the tick saves on the server, so closing the tab does not lose it. A turn reads as untouched, started, or done, and the desk says which. The cleaner can also add a room photo from the phone: a JPEG, PNG, or WebP under 4 MB, at most 12 on one turn, and only for a turn on that cleaner's list; a photo path is readable only if this app would have written it. The host desk counts an uploaded photo, so the turn reads as finished rather than waiting for a photo in the desk's own tab. The link carries no door code, no guest name, and no rate. When saved bookings could not be read, each house still shows checkout at 11:00 AM, parking, quiet hours, house notes, the guest checkout steps, and the standing clean list, in English or Spanish. That card does not name a stay. When checkout mornings can be read, the page lists them and does not name a stay. Nothing was booked or sent. That page does not also say there are no checkouts. When the job cards already list a checkout, the page does not say there are no checkouts. Nothing was booked or sent. The route uses those houses. A house with no checkout is left off. Nothing was booked or sent. A next stay or a checkout that names only children says a stay needs an adult. Names stay off that line. Nothing is sent. Each card says whether quiet hours are in effect in Utah right now, in English or Spanish. The River House guide does not name a clock. That line is not a checklist item. The canyon line does not say that Provo Canyon and Lindon share no day. When checkout mornings can be read, that line uses those mornings. It does not say the list could not be read. Nothing was booked or sent. The drive notes from the published guide still show, and they are not part of the clean checklist. In Spanish, those drive notes and the house notes use the same published facts. The standing list can be checked here. The room-photo step stays open until a photo is in this tab, and that photo is not uploaded. The River House photo line repeats the published bedroom sentence. Each card names the stay-agreement safety line: no lifeguard, an adult around water, and no fireworks. That card does not sign the agreement. That sentence is not a new list. Each card also names the next event the rate card can quote. That card does not name a stay. A note can be saved for the house with no stay attached. A door code and a price stay off that note. Nothing is sent, and it does not change a booking or an expense. The Ranch House and the Lindon House are one trip in Lindon. The River House is a separate trip up Provo Canyon. When a day has both, the desk says the canyon is a separate trip and that the clock does not include the drive. The clock still says whether the turns fit. The guest leaving list adds toilet paper only at the River House and the hot tub cover at the Ranch House. It also says the standing prep: a grocery drop at the River House, the hot tub at the Ranch House, and neither at the Lindon House. The card does not say that anyone asked, and nothing is charged. A same-day turn is 5 hours, from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM. A 1:00 PM arrival makes it 2 hours. A 2:00 PM leave before a 4:00 PM arrival makes it 2 hours. When the turnover list can be read, a checkout note that names a 2:00 PM leave, or a next stay that names a 1:00 PM arrival, uses that shorter clock. A preference card that names 11:00 AM keeps the 11:00 AM start. The rest of the note stays off the job. When two or three houses check out on the same day, the desk says whether those same-day turns overlap. A 1:00 PM arrival and a 2:00 PM leave can fit one after the other when both houses are in Lindon. A River House turn on that day is not treated as that fit, because the drive up Provo Canyon is not in the clock. The co-host brief uses that same clock. A turn with no same-day guest can wait. Nothing is booked or sent. Otherwise, turnovers for the next two weeks, with the address, a map link, parking, house notes, before-you-go drive notes, the guest's quiet hours and no-smoking rule, and the checkout steps the guest was asked to do. Those rules and steps are not the cleaner checklist. The work order names when the next stay starts, when that door code opens, when the next stay covers a named event, how many guests are checking out, how many guests the next booking names, including children when the note names them and they fit inside that guest total, whether that next stay named an arrival time, whether this checkout named a departure time, whether a 2:00 PM leave is open for that checkout, whether the next stay can arrive at 1:00 PM, and whether that stay can request the hot tub or a grocery drop. Names and the code stay off the paper.

- `#/ours` — Brandon & Stephanie household / furnishings (photo, paste text, or manual; off rental P&L)

### JavaScript bridge

```
UML.navigate("construction")
UML.navigate("report", "documents")
UML.setMonth("2026-08")
UML.state()
UML.help()
```

### Login

POST `/api/auth/login` with `{ "password": "..." }` (cookie). Form: `[data-bot="login-password"]` and `[data-bot="login-submit"]`.

Every private route needs a configured `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` plus a matching cookie, or a valid Muse/Amanda bearer. If the deployment has no password, private reads answer 401 with `code: "not-configured"` and the sign-in page says the site is unprotected; it does not treat the caller as the host. The public booking page, `/api/book/availability`, `/api/market/overview`, a guest stay link, and a guest request stay open. The public house guide drops the door code, the Wi-Fi password, its name, and the door notes for a caller who is not signed in. `npm run check:guards` fails the build when a host route loses its guard. A cookie-authenticated response is only readable from the deployed origin or a local dev port: a stranger gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` with no credentials line, and every response carries `Vary: Origin`.

Muse and Amanda have full control with `Authorization: Bearer` `MUSE_BOT_SECRET` or `AMANDA_BOT_SECRET`.
OpenAPI: `/api/muse/openapi.json` and `/api/amanda/openapi.json` — declares every bearer route with its refusals, and the four token-in-the-path routes as public.
Tools: `GET/POST /api/muse/tools` or `/api/amanda/tools`. Use tool `dashboard_request` for any other `/api` route.
Signed-in browser: `/api/muse/enter?token=` or `/api/amanda/enter?token=`.

### Routes a bot can reach

`dashboard_request` forwards the bearer, so the same secret opens every host route below without a cookie.

- `GET /api/book/requests` — saved direct requests with `taken` and `accepted` flags, plus the guest total and a suggested host payout for each, computed from the same quote the guest page uses. `GET/POST /api/book/holds` lists or releases a live hold. `POST /api/book/accept { id, payout }` turns a request into a booking, refuses a second accept or a clashing night, saves a stay on each house a two-house request names. The host net is split in proportion to each house's **lodging**, not its guest total, because cleaning differs per house and is not part of the payout; weighting by the guest total put $121 of a 30-guest booking on the wrong house. A quote that cannot price both falls back to an even split rather than zeroing a house. It also mints the guest `/stay/:token` link and emails the confirmation. **That email is sent by the route, and nothing in the route asks first: the desk's confirm lives in the page, and the agent's lives in its tool. A caller that hits this route directly books and emails in one call.** `POST /api/book/decline { id, reason }` records a decline with a reason, lets the hold go, and tells the guest the dates are not available; a request that is already a booking cannot be declined.
- `GET/POST/DELETE /api/clean/links` — cleaner links. A cleaner link is the credential for `GET /api/clean/:token` (no login), which returns the next two weeks of turns with no door code, guest name, or rate. `POST /api/clean/:token { house, checkout, done:[ids] }` ticks a step. `GET /api/clean/progress` is what cleaners have ticked.
- `GET/POST /api/owner/links` then `GET /api/owner/:token` — a read-only link for Todd. Ranch and River only, after the fee, with no Lindon, household, construction, or guest names.
- `GET /api/pricing/snapshots` and `POST /api/pricing/comp-set` — saved real comps. A comp needs `sleeps` and `distanceMi` to set the rate band. `POST /api/pricing/snapshots { compId, asks: [{ date, nightlyRate }] }` records the guest ask a comp actually lists on a night, up to 120 nights in one save. A comp sets the band only on a night that carries a saved ask, so the POST is what activates the live band; every row is checked before any is written.
- `GET /api/expenses/archive`, `POST /api/expenses/archive?restore=<id>`, and `DELETE /api/expenses/archive?purge=<id>` — host only. A delete writes the row to an archive before removing it, and does not touch storage, so a restore brings the row back with its receipt still readable. The archive is not a second ledger: no total, report, or statement counts it. A delete that cannot be archived does not happen. Purge is the only path that deletes a receipt, and it refuses a live expense.
- `GET/POST /api/stay-guide/:token/stay-message` — host only. Lists the stay messages that are right to send **today**, and sends exactly one, by hand. Nothing is scheduled: no message goes out on its own. Each message has a window measured from check-in or checkout, so a week note cannot go sixty days out and a review ask cannot go before the guest has left. A message already sent for that stay is refused. No price, door code, or password goes out; the messages mention the door code only to say it is not included, so the guard looks for a code given as a value. **A message that points the guest at their stay page is refused while the guest app is off for that house**, because that page answers 403. The stay comes from the guest record behind the token, never from the request body.
- `GET /api/book/request/:token` — where one direct request stands, for the guest who sent it. The token in the path is the whole credential, and it is the only thing this route accepts. It answers `waiting`, `accepted`, `declined`, `expired`, or `cancelled`, with the dates and the party. An `expired` hold does **not** mean nobody answered: the request is still acceptable, and the page says so rather than inviting a second request for the same nights. A cancelled booking is its own state, never "nobody answered". It never returns the guest's name, email, phone, note, or any price, so a forwarded link exposes nothing that was not already on the booking page. The page is `/request/:token`.
- `GET /api/pricing/push-plan` — what a rate push would change. Booked, closed, paused, locked, and held nights are never in it. It answers `sends:false` and has no writer, so no price can leave from it.
- `GET/POST/DELETE /api/pricing/approved-rates` — the one path from the pricing engine to a guest. `POST { house, date, guest }` approves one night, and that night quotes this price on our own page and in the guest month grid. It is refused on a booked, closed, held, or paused night, and outside the floor, the ceiling, the 8% raise cap, and the published 20% promotion. `DELETE ?house=&date=` returns the night to the card. It does not send anything to Airbnb, VRBO, or Hospitable.
- `GET/POST /api/pricing/shadow-days` — the durable seven-day clock. The write token is never returned.
- `GET /api/platform/health`, `GET /api/platform/registry`, `GET /api/platform/status`, and `GET /api/platform/funnel` — host only. Health names which bindings and keys exist and never returns a secret. The registry is the feature catalog with how many rows sit in D1; POST seeds it with an upsert that deletes nothing. Status is the morning list of missing keys. Funnel is counts only, with no address, name, phone, or device. Nothing here sends or charges.
- `GET /api/platform/conditions` — host only. Live snow at Sundance over the next 48 hours, a three-day forecast for each house, any active winter alert, and whether two inches is enough to suggest sending the plow. Read from the National Weather Service, which needs no key. It answers `sends: false` and changes no booking. A failed read says the forecast could not be read — never that the weather is clear. The canyon road line carries a winter alert covering Provo Canyon; a real road feed needs `UDOT_API_KEY` and `UDOT_ROAD_ENDPOINT`, and with neither set the line says the road is not connected rather than implying it is open.
- `GET /api/platform/switches` and `POST /api/platform/switches { id, on }` — host only. Three switches a host may set: `digest` (compose and send the morning text), `snow` (include snow in it), and `shadowDay` (record a shadow day from the morning run instead of waiting for a page visit). `guestAutoReply` and `publishRates` are refused 409 with the reason and are not on the page as controls. A store that cannot be read reports every switch off with `ok: false`, never as deliberately off, and every write is audited.
- `POST /api/platform/daily` — the morning run, and the one route the worker cron calls. It records today's shadow day from the live calendar, builds the morning list (arrivals, departures, and the nights no stay can sell inside 14 days), reads the snow when the `snow` switch is on, and sends **at most one** text to `HOST_DIGEST_TO` per date. A host session may run it by hand to read the text; the worker uses `Authorization: Bearer CRON_SECRET`, which the app accepts **only on this route**, so a leaked cron secret cannot read the books. It refuses to send when the books could not be read, when the switches could not be read, or when a digest already went out today, and every response says which of those happened. It never texts a guest. `GET` on the same path reports the switches, whether Twilio is configured, and whether a recipient is set, and sends nothing.
- `GET /api/platform/funnel?window=7` (or `30`) — host only. One figure per step **counted by visit rather than by row**, so a reload is not a second guest, plus the number of visits that picked dates and never sent. That last figure is what an abandoned quote looks like on this site; no fifth event was invented for it.
- `GET /api/stay-guide/:token/conditions` — public; the stay token is the whole credential, the same as the guide beside it. The three-day forecast and any winter advisory for the house this stay is at. Weather only: no name, no dates, no door code. It never says the canyon road is open.
- `POST /api/funnel` — public. Records one funnel step (`view`, `quote`, `checkout`, `paid`) with a house and an optional random visit id in the market database. No address, name, phone, or device. A step outside those four is refused, and a day at its ceiling is refused rather than filling the table.
- `GET /api/book/quote` — public tax estimate. It is not added to the quoted stay and nothing is charged.
- `GET /api/book/turnstile` — public. The Turnstile site key and whether a bot check is enforced. Never the secret. An unconfigured deployment says so, and the booking route records that no bot check ran rather than claiming one did.
- `POST /api/hooks/hospitable`, `POST /api/hooks/stripe`, and `POST /api/hooks/seam` — signed webhooks. A bad signature is refused. The books are not written.
- `GET/POST /api/pricing/pause` — the per-house pricing kill switch, host only. `POST { house, paused, reason? }` sets one house. The authoritative plan reads it, so a paused house is never raised or promoted. A switch that cannot be read reports **every house paused**, never off; this does not change a published rate and sends nothing.
- `GET /api/pricing/changes` — the rate change log, host only. One row per night whose rate moved, with the reason, newest first. Every row is a shadow row and says nothing was sent. A failed read says the log could not be read rather than showing an empty log.
- `GET /api/platform/audit` — the audit log, admin only. Who changed what and when, newest first. No amount, guest name, phone, or receipt body. A failed read says the log could not be read rather than showing an empty log. An owner account is refused, because the log names work on houses an owner does not see.
- `GET /api/mcp` — read-only tools. Bulk delete is refused.

### Do not

- Put construction partner bills on ranch/lindon/river. Partner spend is construction only.
- Treat Lindon as 50/50 with Todd; Lindon is Brandon’s rental P&L.
- Use Firecrawl unless the user asked.

### Useful APIs (cookie auth)

- GET `/api/portfolio/metrics?month=YYYY-MM`
- GET `/api/expenses`
- POST `/api/expenses` — construction: `propertyId: "construction"`, `paidBy: "brandon"|"todd"`, `stage`
- POST `/api/expenses` — Brandon & Stephanie household: `propertyId: "household"`, `paidBy: "brandon"`, `category` Furnishings/Decor/Supplies/Other
- POST `/api/agent/chat` — rental co-host tools
- POST `/api/agent/construction/chat` — construction manager
- GET `/api/construction/project`
- GET `/api/esign/templates`
- POST `/api/esign/parse-invoice` — import a contractor invoice or email onto a lien waiver (`type`: text / image / gmail / gmail-search)
- GET `/api/surveys` — upcoming stays + preference surveys
- POST `/api/surveys/send` — `{ reservationId? , confirmationCode?, channel: "email"|"sms"|"none" }` mints `/stay/:token`. `none` copies a link for Airbnb paste (does not email/SMS the guest).
- GET/POST `/api/stay-preferences/:token` — public guest survey. River uses the short VIP flow and asks for an arrival time. Choosing a time does not send the form.
